edges.mechanism: Mesembrine is a potent serotonin transporter inhibitor (Ki 1.4 nM; Zembrin IC50 4.3 ug/mL); combining with SSRIs/SNRIs could add serotonergic load and theoretically precipitate serotonin toxicity.
edges.evidence: In vitro binding data plus serotonin-syndrome review and ADDF report advising against co-use; no case reports or combination trials; theoretical, very low certainty.

edges.mechanism: Sceletium extract acts as a monoamine-releasing agent (VMAT-2 up-regulation, SERT down-regulation) with mild MAO-A inhibition, and sub-fractions inhibit MAO-B; additive serotonergic/monoaminergic effects with MAOIs are plausible.
edges.evidence: Cell-based mechanistic studies and serotonin-syndrome review; combination never studied; theoretical.

edges.mechanism: Serotonin syndrome can arise from interactions between two or more serotonergic agents; Zembrin alkaloids inhibit SERT.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference from in vitro SERT data and a focused review of serotonin syndrome; no clinical reports.

edges.mechanism: Zembrin and mesembrenone inhibit PDE4 selectively; additive PDE4 inhibition could increase PDE4-inhibitor effects (GI upset, insomnia, psychiatric signals reported for roflumilast).
edges.evidence: In vitro enzyme data; ADDF report lists roflumilast as a mechanism-based interaction; roflumilast FAERS analysis for adverse-effect profile; no interaction study.

edges.mechanism: No hepatic CYP inhibition/induction data exist for Zembrin or mesembrine; alkaloids undergo oxidative O-/N-demethylation and hydroxylation in human liver preparations, and a high-mesembrine extract inhibited steroidogenic CYP17 in adrenal cells.
edges.evidence: Data gap: metabolism study (rat urine, human liver preparations) and in vitro adrenal steroidogenesis study only; interaction potential unknown.

edges.mechanism: A Sceletium alkaloid fraction caused ataxia in rats and traditional tinctures were used for sedation; additive CNS depression is plausible (mechanistic inference).
edges.evidence: Rat behavioural study and ethnobotanical review; no human interaction data.

edges.mechanism: Historical (1789) and contemporary user reports describe synergism and potentiation of smoked cannabis by Sceletium/kougoed.
edges.evidence: Anecdotal reports collated in an ethnobotanical review; no controlled data.

edges.mechanism: Some commercial kanna products contain the phenethylamine alkaloid hordenine, and one was adulterated with ephedrine; additive sympathomimetic effects possible with non-standardized products.
edges.evidence: Forensic product analyses; not applicable to verified standardized Zembrin.

edges.mechanism: Additive serotonergic load with SERT-inhibiting alkaloids (mechanistic inference).
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference only, cited to SERT data and serotonin-syndrome review.

edges.mechanism: No human or reproductive-toxicology data; trials enrolled only healthy non-pregnant adults; toxicology data are limited.
edges.evidence: Absence of data (RCT inclusion, bibliometric review of gaps, ADDF report).

edges.with: treated depression, anxiety or bipolar disorder
edges.mechanism: Psychoactive serotonergic/PDE4 agent never tested in clinical psychiatric populations; agitation, irritability and depressed mood were reported as possibly related AEs in the safety RCT.
edges.evidence: Reviews note no trials in clinical populations; single small safety RCT.

edges.mechanism: Mesembrine and mesembrenone metabolites are detectable by standard GC-MS/LC-MS urine screening and forensic NACE-MS; no immunoassay cross-reactivity data.
edges.evidence: Analytical/forensic method studies; detection rather than false positives.
